hypothesis.title: Turn on the never-exercised config-scoring feedback path in the graded general config
hypothesis.description: feedback config-scoring is unexercised (cfg_score_sum = 0 under every loop config). Set `feedback.config_scoring = true` in scheduler_configs/loop/general_vr.json (the config the evaluator actually grades - NOT a new variant file, which the pinned eval driver would never run), plus a <20-line wiring fix at the feedback-mode parse site if the flag is not threaded. Default stays false everywhere else. Interpretability precondition: `cfg_score_sum > 0` and `cfg_score_updates > 0` in the recorded metrics; if they stay zero the mechanism is miswired and the correct follow-up is ablation of the path, not tuning.
hypothesis.rationale: This is the only inter-run adaptation lever in the simulator that has never been switched on, and the standing mechanism-liveness rule says nothing may build on cfg-scoring until it is enabled in general_vr.json. Every falsified family so far operated within a run (perturbation volume, delivery ordering, receiver-side holding, coverage resolution); config-scoring reallocates effort across runs, a structurally different lever. Either it moves nothing and the path joins the zero-utilization ablation sweep - retiring a whole config surface - or it moves and opens a family no prior hypothesis could touch.
hypothesis.generalityArgument: Switches on a generic cross-run configuration reweighting mechanism; the flag names no handler, timer, or protocol role, and enabling a mechanism in the subject config is explicitly in bounds.
hypothesis.notes: Falsifier: if cfg_score_sum/cfg_score_updates remain 0 after enabling, the mechanism is dead code - reject and route to ablation. If live, pre-register P(depth>=4) ratio >= 1.05 against the +0.07% null floor; below that, the mechanism fires but is unrewarding and dependent proposals are barred.
